propositions: A deterministic clarity floor must distinguish structural plan-executability failures from advisory style preferences, using closed-ticket counterexamples to eliminate false positives.

Nonempty parsed Acceptance Criteria checkbox items and unresolved sentinel assignments in active execution sections are retained as hard-floor rules after adversarial historical search found no legitimate counterexamples.

Exact duplicate Acceptance Criteria, preferred section presence, file-impact schema validation, and rebar citation edge-checking are reclassified as write-schema invariants or advisory signals, not raw clarity rules.

The revised floor rejects the undefined historical-section exclusion and replaces it with deterministic boundary-checking: exact current headings for sentinel rules, explicit structural forms (unresolved value positions) with negation suppression, and continuation-joining for AC items.

Five candidate rules underwent adversarial counterexample search in the signed+completed corpus; two were retained hard, three were narrowed or removed, with specific control tickets (c244, 8d27, 6673, 94f9) designated for validation.

The final framework separates eight candidate signals into hard-floor (2), write-schema (1), grounding-path (1), and advisory-only (4) categories, with explicit before/after detection wording documenting each change.
